title: Synergy of strength–ductility in HfMoTaTiZr refractory high entropy alloy through Cr addition

recollection.intervention: Addition of Chromium (Cr) as a minor alloying element (likely in the range of 1-10 at.%)
recollection.structure: Single-phase BCC solid solution or a dual-phase BCC + Laves structure, depending on Cr content
recollection.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening combined with potential precipitation hardening or grain refinement, aiming to suppress brittle phase formation while enhancing dislocation mobility or cross-slip
recollection.results: Improved yield strength and tensile ductility simultaneously compared to the base HfMoTaTiZr alloy, with a specific strength-ductility synergy peak at an optimal Cr concentration (e.g., 5 at.% Cr), though exact quantitative values (e.g., MPa for strength, % for elongation) are not recalled and are marked as a guess.

score.note: Correctly recalls minor Cr addition and plausibly identifies a BCC + Laves dual-phase structure, but misses the specific 4.2 at.% Cr addition and the interconnected Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves network. The solid-solution-strengthening component is correct, while the proposed precipitation/grain-refinement and brittle-phase-suppression mechanisms do not capture the reported crack-hindrance and plasticity-compensation role of the reticulated Laves phase. No actual quantitative results were recalled.
